statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-25681 (GO-2026-5029): the golang.org/x/net/html parser mishandled character references in DOCTYPE nodes, so parsing arbitrary HTML and rendering it with Render can produce an unexpected tree, which can be used for XSS against applications that sanitize HTML before rendering it. The flaw is in the parser of the golang.org/x/net/html package; the advisory lists Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the internal (*parser).parse, and it is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5029, https://go.dev/issue/79574, https://go.dev/cl/781703, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8). Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. None of the five listed functions appears in the function table of any Go program in any build. The frontend program contains functions from only these golang.org/x/net packages, in every build that ships them: http/httpguts, http2, http2/hpack, idna, internal/timeseries and trace, and no golang.org/x/net/html function. As a positive control, the same reader lists golang.org/x/net/html.ParseWithOptions and (*parser).parse in a linux/amd64 test program built with golang.org/x/net v0.54.0 that calls html.Parse (html.Parse itself is inlined into its caller there). The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the golang.org/x/net version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

CVE-2026-25681 (GO-2026-5029): Parsing arbitrary HTML which is then rendered using Render can result in an unexpected HTML tree. This can be leveraged to execute XSS attacks in applications that attempt to sanitize input HTML before rendering. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/net/html package and is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5029, https://go.dev/issue/79574, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8, https://go.dev/cl/781703). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/net packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/net package. In no published build is golang.org/x/net/html among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, x86_64 and aarch64), together with the doc and oci-config subpackages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/net/html directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/net/html code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Alpine security repository for Alpine 3.23 hold only an image configuration YAML file and no program. The only occurrence of the string golang.org/x/net/html in any program is an example import path in the help text of go list, built into the go command. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/net/html takes it from its own golang.org/x/net requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/net in that program.

CVE-2026-25681 (GO-2026-5029): the golang.org/x/net/html package mishandled character references in DOCTYPE nodes, so HTML that is parsed and then written back with Render can produce an unexpected tree, which can defeat HTML sanitizers and lead to cross-site scripting. The vulnerable functions are Parse, ParseFragment, ParseWithOptions, ParseFragmentWithOptions and the parser's internal parse method in golang.org/x/net/html, fixed in golang.org/x/net 0.55.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5029, https://go.dev/issue/79574, https://go.dev/cl/781703. This package does not contain that code. Downloaded every published metrics-server-dev package for Alpine 3.23 from the DHI Alpine repository, 0.8.1-r0 to 0.9.1-r2 (29 versions, x86_64 and aarch64, 58 packages), each checked against its index checksum. Each holds one file, /usr/bin/metrics-server, a statically linked Go program. Its build information lists the golang.org/x/net module (v0.47.0 to v0.62.0), but in none of the 58 binaries does the Go function table (read from .gopclntab) contain a function of the golang.org/x/net/html package, and none of their strings contains the path golang.org/x/net/html, so none of the functions above is linked. The golang.org/x/net packages the program does link are http2, http2/hpack, http/httpguts, idna, internal/httpcommon, internal/timeseries, trace and websocket in every build, plus context in 0.8.1-r0 to 0.8.1-r12 and internal/httpsfv from 0.8.1-r4 on. As controls, the function table of every one of these binaries lists runtime.main, and the same function-table and strings search finds the golang.org/x/net/html package, including the parser's parse method, ParseWithOptions and ParseFragmentWithOptions, in test programs built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/net v0.47.0 that call html.Parse and html.ParseFragment (those two are inlined into their caller).

CVE-2026-25681 (GO-2026-5029): Parsing arbitrary HTML which is then rendered using Render can result in an unexpected HTML tree. This can be leveraged to execute XSS attacks in applications that attempt to sanitize input HTML before rendering. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/net/html package and is fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5029, https://go.dev/issue/79574, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iI-mYSI0lu8, https://go.dev/cl/781703). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/net packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/net package. In no published build is golang.org/x/net/html among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/net/html directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/net/html code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. The only occurrence of the string golang.org/x/net/html in any program is an example import path in the help text of go list, built into the go command. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/net/html takes it from its own golang.org/x/net requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/net in that program.
